name: 203 - Holdouts - Held-Out Unit Suppresses Covered Experiment
description: A unit landing in a holdout's variant 0 gets control values for the experiment it covers (no exposure of its own) and exactly one ordinary exposure for the holdout itself.

name: 204 - Holdouts - Not-Held-Out Unit Assigns Normally And Exposes Holdout
description: A unit outside the holdout's suppressed arm assigns to the covered experiment exactly as it would without holdouts, plus one ordinary exposure for the holdout carrying its nonzero (not-held-out) variant.

name: 205 - Holdouts - Union Of Two Holdouts Suppresses Via Higher-Id Holdout
description: An experiment covered by two holdouts is suppressed if the unit is held out by EITHER one (union semantics). Pinned so the low-id holdout does NOT hold the unit out and the high-id holdout does, ruling out an implementation that only ever consults holdouts[0]. Both holdouts still emit their own independent exposure.

name: 206 - Holdouts - Coverage Is Opt-In Per Experiment
description: Holdout coverage never leaks to a sibling experiment lacking holdoutIds, even when that sibling shares the same unit and context as an experiment the same holdout suppresses.

name: 207 - Holdouts - Dangling Holdout Id Ignored, Valid Coverage Still Applies
description: A holdoutIds entry with no matching holdouts[] element is silently ignored - wire inconsistency tolerance, not an error - while a second, valid id in the same list still applies normally.

name: 208 - Holdouts - Suppresses Full-On Experiment Regardless Of Full-On Variant
description: A holdout suppresses a full-on experiment (fullOnVariant != 0) exactly as it does a traffic-eligible one - explicit holdoutIds coverage, not full-on status, decides suppression.

name: 209 - Holdouts - Old-Payload Tolerance For Uncovered Experiment
description: INERTNESS BASELINE (must pass on every SDK, holdout-aware or not): holdouts[] is present in the payload but the experiment under test declares no holdoutIds, so behavior is identical whether or not the SDK understands the holdouts wire format at all. Contrasts with the other Holdouts scenarios in this group, which fail on any SDK that has not implemented holdout resolution.

name: 210 - Holdout - Override Takes Precedence Over Holdout
description: An explicit override wins over holdout membership for the experiment's own assignment; the override path still evaluates coverage, so the holdout's own exposure fires alongside it

name: 211 - Holdout - Holdout Takes Precedence Over Custom Assignment
description: Holdout membership forces control and suppresses the experiment's own exposure even with a custom assignment on file; only the holdout's own exposure fires

name: 212 - Holdout - Independent Holdouts Across Experiments
description: Same unit is held out for one experiment's holdout but not another's, using independent seeds; the held-out experiment fires no exposure of its own while the non-held-out one does

name: 213 - Holdout - Consistent Membership Across Shared Holdout
description: Same unit and same shared holdout definition produce consistent holdout membership across different experiments; the shared holdout's own exposure fires once on first evaluation and neither covered experiment fires its own exposure

name: 214 - Holdout Arms - Three-Arm Variant 0 Holds Out Full-On And Non-Full-On (uid e791e240fcd3df7d238cfc285f475e8152fcc0ec)
description: A 3-arm holdout's variant 0 forces control for every covered experiment, full-on or not, identically to a 2-arm holdout's variant 0; the holdout's own exposure fires once at variant 0 and neither covered experiment emits its own exposure.

name: 215 - Holdout Arms - Three-Arm Variant 1 Holds Out Non-Full-On, Assigns Full-On Normally (uid e791e240fcd3df7d238cfc285f475e8152fcc0ec)
description: A 3-arm holdout's variant 1 forces control only for a covered experiment with fullOnVariant==0; a covered full-on experiment (fullOnVariant!=0) takes its normal assignment path and is assigned its own fullOnVariant with fullOn=true, not suppressed.

name: 216 - Holdout Arms - Three-Arm Variant 2 Evaluates Both Experiments Normally (uid e791e240fcd3df7d238cfc285f475e8152fcc0ec)
description: A 3-arm holdout's variant 2 (normal traffic) evaluates every covered experiment exactly as if uncovered, full-on or not; the holdout's own exposure fires once at variant 2.

name: 217 - Holdout Arms - Three-Arm Variant 1 Defers To Normal Path For Audience Mismatch (uid e791e240fcd3df7d238cfc285f475e8152fcc0ec)
description: A full-on experiment covered by a 3-arm holdout's variant 1 is not short-circuited to its fullOnVariant: audienceStrict is evaluated first, so an audience mismatch still forces control (not suppression) with assigned=false and audienceMismatch=true; the experiment's own exposure fires because it was evaluated and rejected by audience, not held out.

name: 218 - Holdout Arms - Three-Arm Variant 2 Audience Mismatch Matches Variant 1 Verdict (uid e791e240fcd3df7d238cfc285f475e8152fcc0ec)
description: The same full-on/audience-mismatch experiment, covered instead by the 3-arm holdout's variant 2 (normal traffic), yields the identical verdict as scenario 217's variant 1: control, assigned=false, audienceMismatch=true. This pins that arm 1 defers to the normal assignment path instead of short-circuiting to the full-on variant.

name: 219 - Holdout Arms - Union Two-Arm Holds Out While Applicable Three-Arm Does Not (uid e791e240fcd3df7d238cfc285f475e8152fcc0ec)
description: A covered experiment is suppressed if EITHER applicable holdout holds it out, even when a 3-arm holdout's own arm (variant 2, normal traffic) would not have held it out on its own; both holdouts still emit their own independent exposure with their own variant. A second experiment covered only by the non-suppressing 3-arm holdout takes its normal assignment path and emits its own exposure, proving that holdout 22's arm is not itself suppressing.

name: 220 - Holdout Arms - Union Three-Arm Variant 1 Holds Out While Applicable Two-Arm Does Not (uid e791e240fcd3df7d238cfc285f475e8152fcc0ec)
description: Union, the other direction: a 3-arm holdout's variant 1 holds a non-full-on covered experiment out even when an applicable 2-arm holdout alone would not have; both holdouts still emit their own independent exposure with their own variant. A second experiment covered only by the non-suppressing 2-arm holdout takes its normal assignment path and emits its own exposure, proving that holdout 11's arm is not itself suppressing.

name: 221 - Holdouts - Late Unit Publishes Previously Unavailable Holdout Exposure
description: A covered full-on experiment can resolve before its unit type is installed; after setUnit supplies that unit, resolving it again publishes the holdout exposure that was unavailable during the first evaluation.

name: 222 - Holdout Arms - Three-Arm Arity Derived From Split Without holdoutType (uid e791e240fcd3df7d238cfc285f475e8152fcc0ec)
description: Identical to the three-arm variant 0 scenario, but the holdout definition omits the holdoutType field entirely. An SDK must derive the holdout's arm count from its split length alone, so suppression of both the full-on and non-full-on covered experiments is unchanged. Pins that holdoutType is not required on the wire.

name: 223 - Holdouts - Exposure State Survives Publish
description: Holdout and experiment exposures are once per context, not once per publish: after the queue is flushed, calling treatment again on the same experiment, or on another experiment covered by the same holdout, queues nothing. Covers both a held-out holdout (suppressed experiments) and a not-held-out one (normal experiment exposure plus holdout exposure).

name: 224 - Holdouts - Refresh Keeps Exposure Unless Holdout Iteration Changes
description: A refresh with identical data keeps the holdout's exposure state, so neither the covered experiment nor a sibling covered by the same holdout re-exposes it. A refresh that bumps the holdout's iteration starts a new epoch: the next covered treatment publishes one new holdout exposure, and the sibling then shares it.

name: 225 - Holdouts - Refresh Adding Or Removing Coverage Re-Resolves Experiment
description: An experiment's holdout set is part of its assignment epoch. A refresh that adds a held-out holdout to holdoutIds re-resolves an already-exposed experiment: it is suppressed to control and the holdout exposure fires. A refresh that removes the coverage again restores its normal assignment with a fresh experiment exposure.

name: 226 - Holdouts - Variable Value Of Suppressed Experiment Returns Control
description: For a held-out unit, variableValue on a covered experiment returns the control variant's value (not the caller's default and not the unit's would-be treatment value), peekVariableValue does the same without queuing anything, and the first variableValue fires only the holdout's exposure. A later treatment call on the same experiment queues nothing.

name: 227 - Holdouts - Holdout Resolves Per Covered Experiment Unit Type
description: A holdout is evaluated with the covered experiment's unitType, not the holdout's own declared unitType (matching the java-sdk reference implementation). One holdout covering experiments of two unit types therefore yields one exposure per unit type, each carrying that unit; a second experiment of an already-exposed unit type would not re-expose it.

name: 228 - Switchback - Golden Vectors - assignSwitchback - 2 Arms

name: 243 - Switchback - Units In One Bucket Share The Variant
description: Two experiments with the same seed and switchbackClusterCount 10 on different unit types. Both uids hash into bucket 4, so both serve the bucket's period-0 variant 1, while per-value clustering on the two hashed uids would serve different variants.

name: 244 - Switchback - Ineligible - exp_switchback_pre_anchor
description: switchbackStartAt 4102444800000 (2100-01-01T00:00Z) is after now, so the experiment is ineligible: variant 0 with assigned=true, eligible=false, exposed once and never drawn from split/seed.

name: 245 - Switchback - Ineligible - exp_switchback_no_anchor
description: switchbackStartAt is absent (an experiment that has not started), so the grid cannot be evaluated: variant 0 with assigned=true, eligible=false, exposed once.

name: 246 - Switchback - Unassigned - Cluster Unit Not Set
description: The context has no warehouse_id unit, so the switchback experiment is unassigned: variant 0 with assigned=false and eligible=true, and no fallback to any other unit.

name: 247 - Switchback - Ineligible - Cluster Count Not 10, 50 Or 100
description: switchbackClusterCount absent, and switchbackClusterCount 1000: only 10, 50 and 100 are servable, so each experiment is ineligible (variant 0, assigned=true, eligible=false, exposed once) and never falls back to per-value clustering or to another count. The uid draws nonzero under every allowed count and under sticky unit assignment.

name: 248 - Switchback - Same Period - Exactly One Exposure
description: Two getTreatment calls within one period return the same variant and expose once.

name: 249 - Switchback - Full-On Serves The Full-On Variant
description: fullOnVariant=2 takes precedence over the switchback draw: variant 2 with fullOn=true.

name: 250 - Switchback - Override Wins Over The Switchback Draw
description: The period-0 draw for this cluster is 2; an override to 1 is served instead with assigned=false and overridden=true.

name: 251 - Switchback - Exposure And Publish Payload Carry No New Fields
description: A unit experiment on the same cluster unit is exposed and published first as the baseline. The switchback exposure and its publish event must then have exactly the baseline's fields at every depth (sameShapeAs), with every exposure field value pinned, so a switchback-only field such as a period index fails the scenario.

name: 252 - Switchback - Attribute Source - String, Whole Number, Nested And Array-Index Paths
description: Four attribute-sourced switchbacks on one store_id unit: switchbackClusterAttribute "city" (a top-level string, 100 buckets), "store_number" (a whole number above 2^31, keyed as its base-10 string, 50 buckets), "geo/city" (a nested key, 10 buckets) and "items/0/city" (an array index between two keys, 100 buckets). Each variant is assignSwitchback(str(bucketOf(key, seed, count)), 0, seed, arms); every value is chosen so that variant is nonzero and differs from the unit-sourced draw, from the sticky unit assignment, from per-value clustering on the key, from the other counts and from a little-endian bucket, and items[1].city would draw differently from items[0].city. The whole number's int32 wrap and its double renderings ("<n>.0", "<m>E9", "<m>e+09") would each serve a different variant.

name: 253 - Switchback - Attribute Source - No Bucket Key Is Ineligible
description: Attribute-sourced switchbacks whose key is missing (never set), an empty string, a non-integral number (1.5), a boolean, an object, or behind the unsupported path "items/-1/city" (a negative index). Each serves variant 0 with assigned=true and eligible=false, exposed once, and never falls back to the unit. Count and arms per experiment are chosen so that the unit-sourced draw and every lax reading of the value ("1.5", "true", the last array element, ...) would serve a nonzero variant. An integral float such as 2.0 is not a case here: JSON-number runtimes (JavaScript and its frameworks) cannot tell 2.0 from 2. The integral-float rule is covered by bucket-golden-vectors.json attributeKeys and each typed SDK's own suite.

name: 254 - Switchback - Attribute Source - Platform Attribute Path Cases
description: Every case of the platform's attribute-path-cases.json, one experiment per path, with the fixture's attributes set as top-level attributes, plus two index-position cases over tags=["a","b"] and m=[[{"city":"x"}]]: "tags/0" (an index at the tail) and "m/0/0/city" (two indices in a row) are unsupported although a lax reader would resolve them to "a" and "x". A supported path that resolves to a value is served from that value's bucket; an unsupported path (a negative or misplaced index) or a path that resolves to nothing ("+0" and "\u0660" are keys, not indices) is ineligible. Count and arms per experiment are chosen so an eligible case draws nonzero and unlike the unit-sourced draw, the sticky unit assignment, per-value clustering, the other counts and a little-endian bucket, and unlike as many other leaves as possible; an ineligible case sits where every leaf and the unit would draw nonzero.

name: 255 - Switchback - Attribute Source - Mid-Period setAttribute Keeps The Bucket
description: city='first-13' draws variant 7. setAttribute(city, 'second-0') later in the same period would draw 3, but the period's bucket is already fixed: the treatment stays the same with no new exposure. A non-strict audience flip (tier gold → silver) then re-resolves the slot and re-exposes with audienceMismatch=true, still on the first bucket. The next period reads the attribute again (not testable without clock control).

name: 256 - Switchback - Attribute Source - Attribute Set After An Ineligible Read Does Not Reassign Within The Period
description: zone is unset at the first treatment, so the period resolves ineligible (variant 0, eligible=false). setAttribute(zone, 'zone-12'), which would draw 9, does not reassign within the period: the treatment stays 0 with no new exposure.

name: 257 - Switchback - Inertness - Unit Experiments Unaffected By Switchback Data
description: INERTNESS BASELINE (must pass on every SDK, switchback-aware or not): the payload carries a switchback experiment and unit experiments, two of which also carry every switchback wire field, switchbackClusterCount and switchbackClusterAttribute included (one with randomizationType "unit", one with it absent). Each unit experiment's treatment, exposure and published exposure equal plain unit assignment in every field, the uid is chosen so the switchback draw would differ, and each exposure and publish event has exactly the fields of the plain unit experiment's at every depth. The switchback experiment is never queried: an SDK without switchback serves it a sticky unit assignment that is documented and SDK-specific.
